generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

To find the inverse of the function \(h(x)=\displaystyle {@quest_func@}\), we proceed as follows;

Replace \(h(x)\) with \(y\)

\(\begin{align} y=\displaystyle {@quest_func@}\\ &y({@const_3-const_4*%e^x@})={@const_1+const_2*%e^x@}\\ &{@(const_3*y-y*const_4*%e^x)@}={@const_1+const_2*%e^x@}\\ &{@const_3*y-const_1@}={@const_2*%e^x+y*const_4*%e^x@}\\ &{@const_3*y-const_1@}=e^x({@const_2+y*const_4@})\\ &\displaystyle \frac{{@const_3*y-const_1@}}{{@const_2+y*const_4@}}=e^x\\ \end{align}\)

Rearranging, we have

\(\begin{align} &e^x=\displaystyle \frac{{@const_3*y-const_1@}}{{@const_2+y*const_4@}}\\ &x={@log@} \displaystyle \left ( \frac{{@const_3*y-const_1@}}{{@const_2+y*const_4@}}\right )\\ \end{align}\)

Replacing \(y\) with \(x\) to find the inverse we have;

\(y={@log@} \displaystyle \left ( \frac{{@const_3*x-const_1@}}{{@const_2+x*const_4@}}\right )\)

Therefore, the inverse of the function \(h(x)\) is

\(h^{-1}(x)={@log@} \displaystyle \left ( \frac{{@const_3*x-const_1@}}{{@const_2+x*const_4@}}\right )\)
